messages.speaker: Professor Chen
messages.text: Seventh protocol. An outside signal answers the sounds it makes. It does not follow only the creature's frequency: it also syncs with your heartbeat.

messages.speaker: Professor Chen
messages.text: Something is speaking to the bond between you. What do you do with this signal?

choices.label: I jam the signal before it takes control of the bond.
I request a signal analysis before any answer.
I let it listen to see whether it recognizes the call.

messages.speaker: Professor Chen
messages.text: The signal sends an image: an open corridor, outside air, then a silhouette waiting beyond the complex.

messages.speaker: Professor Chen
messages.text: For us, it may be an invitation or a trap. For the creature, it already feels like a real place: do you cut contact, answer, or follow the image?

choices.label: I close the channel. It is not ready to believe this image.
I answer with a neutral signal, without giving the lab coordinates.
I follow the image with it to understand what is calling.

messages.speaker: Professor Chen
messages.text: If this signal is calling the creature, who has the right to answer: the laboratory, you, or the creature?

choices.label: The laboratory answers. Nobody leaves while the risk exists.
I answer with it, without promising to hand it over.
It answers. If it came from somewhere, it deserves to know.

messages.speaker: Professor Chen
messages.text: You treat the unknown as an intrusion. It is prudent, but it may hear your prudence as fear.

messages.speaker: Professor Chen
messages.text: I would have asked the same thing. Before answering a signal, we verify what it really contains.

messages.speaker: Professor Chen
messages.text: There, you stop speaking in its place. The laboratory is going to hate that answer.
